---
title: "Start your coding agent"
description: "Install Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity on the hub, sign in with your own subscription, and add the ocean-icechunks skills."
---

In this hackathon you hand most of the work to a coding agent running in a hub
terminal. **Bring your own subscription.** Any one of these works:

| Agent | Subscription | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Claude Pro or Max | `claude` |
| OpenAI Codex | ChatGPT Plus or Pro | `codex` |
| Google Antigravity | A Google account with Antigravity access | `agy` |

You install the agent **once**. It goes in `~/.local/bin`, inside your home
directory, so it is still there the next time your server starts. Your sign-in
is saved there too.

::: {.callout-warning}
The agent works in your name, with your subscription. It can read and change
files in your home directory, and it asks before running commands it is not
sure about. Read what it proposes before you say yes.
:::

## 1 · Install and sign in

Open a terminal (**File → New → Terminal**). Then follow the steps for your
agent.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Claude Code

Install:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

Start it:

```bash
cd ~
claude
```

The first start asks you to pick a theme and a sign-in method. Choose **Claude
account with subscription**. It prints a link: open it in your browser, sign
in, and paste the code it gives you back into the terminal.

### Codex

Install it into your home directory. Without `--prefix`, it is installed
somewhere that is wiped when your server restarts.

```bash
npm install -g --prefix ~/.local @openai/codex
```

Sign in. The hub has no browser of its own, so use the device-code flow:

```bash
codex login --device-auth
```

Open the link it prints, sign in with your ChatGPT account, and enter the code.
Then start it:

```bash
cd ~
codex
```

### Antigravity

Install:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash
```

Start it:

```bash
cd ~
agy
```

On the first start, sign in with the Google account that has your Antigravity
access. It prints a link: open it, sign in, approve, and paste the code back
into the terminal.

:::

When you see the agent's prompt, type `/exit` to leave. You only needed it
installed and signed in.

::: {.callout-tip}
## "Command not found"?
Open a **new** terminal, so it picks up `~/.local/bin`. If that does not help,
run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` and try again.
:::

## 2 · Add the ocean-icechunks skills

The [ocean-icechunks-skills](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/ocean-icechunks-skills)
teach your agent how to build, check and document virtual Icechunk stores. This
installs them for all three agents at once:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/ocean-icechunks-skills ~/ocean-icechunks-skills

for dir in ~/.claude/skills ~/.agents/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills; do
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  for skill in virtual-icechunk archive-to-cloud; do
    ln -sfn ~/ocean-icechunks-skills/skills/$skill "$dir/$skill"
  done
done
```

To update them later, run `git -C ~/ocean-icechunks-skills pull`.

## 3 · Start it where you work

An agent works in the folder you start it from. So always `cd` into your
project first:

```bash
cd ~/my-project
claude        # or codex, or agy
```

The first time you start it in a new folder, it asks whether you **trust** the
folder. Say yes for your own project folders.

Check that the skills loaded. Type `/skills` (in Claude Code or Codex) or `/`
(in Antigravity) and look for `virtual-icechunk`. Or just ask: *"What skills do
you have for Icechunk?"*

Chapter 3, [Working with an agent](../slides/03-agent-and-skills.qmd), covers
how to get good work out of it.
